description: KPIECE (Kinodynamic Planning by Interior-Exterior Cell Exploration) grows a tree of motions for a robot that must obey its dynamics (a *kinodynamic* problem). It applies random controls and simulates them forward, so it needs no steering function and no state sampler. A grid over a low-dimensional *projection* of the state, for example the position, records where the tree has been: a cell with all its grid neighbours occupied is *interior*, any other cell is *exterior*, the frontier. KPIECE prefers exterior cells that are little covered and that gave good expansions, so the tree spreads quickly into new space. It is probabilistically complete (it finds a path with probability one, given enough time, if one exists) but not optimal, and it stops at the first motion that reaches the goal. The projection grid can have several levels, after the multi-level discretization of Şucan and Kavraki: each coarser level has cells a fixed ratio larger per axis, and each coarse cell holds the finer cells inside it. Selection then descends from the coarsest level, choosing a cell among the coarsest cells and then among the chosen cell's children, each time with the same exterior rule and importance ranking within that level. Coverage, selection counts and score updates apply to the finest cell and every cell enclosing it. With one level the planner is the single-level one.
